en.name: Almond butter
en.summary: Almond butter keeps about 1 year in the pantry. Stored there it may go hard and the natural oil may separate and float to the top; that is perfectly normal, and stirring it back in — by hand or with a hand mixer — is all that is needed.
en.pantry: A cool, dark cupboard gives about 1 year. The oil separating out is not a fault: almond butter with nothing added has no emulsifier holding it together, so the oil rises and the solids pack down, and the jar goes hard. Mix it manually or with a hand mixer to reincorporate the natural almond oils and it is as it was. Do not pour the oil off, tempting though it looks — that oil is what keeps the rest spreadable, and a jar you have poured will set like concrete. Keep it away from the stove, since heat is what eventually turns the oil rancid.
en.fridge: No refrigerator timeline is published for almond butter, so none is given here. Refrigeration is a reasonable habit in a hot kitchen, and it slows both the separation and the slow oxidation of the oil — the cost is that cold almond butter is very hard to spread, so most people stir the jar, keep it in the cupboard, and simply buy a size they will finish. If you do refrigerate it, stir it thoroughly before it goes in rather than after.
en.freezer: No freezer figure is given for almond butter, and there is little reason to freeze it: a year in the cupboard already outlasts most jars. Freezing does not damage it — it will be safe indefinitely at −18 °C (0 °F) — but it separates further on thawing and needs a determined stir. If you grind your own in quantity, freezing portions is defensible; for a shop jar it is not worth the trouble.
en.thawing: If a jar has been frozen, thaw it in the fridge or at cool room temperature and stir it back together thoroughly before use.
spoilage: A sharp, bitter or paint-like smell — the oil has gone rancid, which is how almond butter ends.
A bitter aftertaste that was not there when the jar was opened.
Mould at the surface or around the rim, usually from a wet or dirty spoon.
A fermented or alcoholic smell, which points to moisture getting in.
tips: Stir the separated oil back in; never pour it off.
Use a clean dry knife every time — moisture is what starts mould.
Store the jar upside down between uses to redistribute the oil.
Keep it away from the hob; heat is what turns the oil.

faq.q: How long does almond butter keep?
faq.a: About 1 year in a cool, dark cupboard. Separation and hardening along the way are normal.

faq.q: Why has my almond butter separated?
faq.a: There is no emulsifier in it, so the natural oil rises. Stir it back in by hand or with a hand mixer.

faq.q: Does almond butter need to be refrigerated?
faq.a: No, the cupboard figure assumes it is not. The fridge slows separation but makes it very hard to spread.

zh.name: 杏仁醬
zh.summary: 杏仁醬放常溫櫥櫃大約可放 1 年。放在那裡它可能會變硬，天然油脂也可能分離浮到表面；那完全正常，用手或手持攪拌機把它拌回去就好。
zh.pantry: 陰涼避光的櫥櫃大約 1 年。油脂分離不是瑕疵：不加任何添加物的杏仁醬沒有乳化劑維繫，所以油會浮上來、固形物往下壓實，整罐變硬。用手或手持攪拌機把天然杏仁油重新拌勻，它就和原本一樣了。不要把油倒掉，不管它看起來多礙眼——那些油正是讓其餘部分還抹得開的東西，倒掉之後整罐會硬得像水泥。另外請遠離爐火，高溫才是最終讓油脂走油耗的原因。
zh.fridge: 杏仁醬沒有公布的冷藏期限，所以本頁不給。在悶熱的廚房裡冷藏是合理的習慣，能同時延緩油脂分離和緩慢氧化——代價是冰過的杏仁醬非常難抹，所以多數人的做法是把罐子拌勻、放櫥櫃，並且買自己吃得完的尺寸。真要冷藏的話，請在放進冰箱之前就充分拌勻，而不是之後才拌。
zh.freezer: 這裡沒有給杏仁醬的冷凍數字，而且也沒什麼理由冷凍：櫥櫃裡的一年已經比大多數罐子的消耗速度長。冷凍不會傷害它——在 −18 °C 下安全性是無限期的——但解凍後會分離得更嚴重，得很用力攪。如果你是自己大量現磨，分份冷凍說得過去；市售一罐就不值得這麼麻煩。
zh.thawing: 如果整罐冷凍過，請放冷藏或涼爽室溫解凍，使用前充分攪拌均勻。
spoilage: 聞起來刺鼻、發苦或有油漆味——油脂走油耗，這也是杏仁醬的結局。
出現剛開罐時沒有的苦後味。
表面或罐口長霉，通常來自沾濕或不乾淨的湯匙。
有發酵味或酒精味，代表水分跑進去了。
tips: 把分離的油拌回去，絕對不要倒掉。
每次都用乾淨乾燥的刀；水分正是發霉的起點。
兩次使用之間把罐子倒放，油脂會重新分布。
遠離爐台；讓油脂變質的就是高溫。

faq.a: 陰涼避光的櫥櫃約 1 年。期間出現分離和變硬都是正常的。

faq.q: 我的杏仁醬為什麼分層了？
faq.a: 因為裡面沒有乳化劑，天然油脂會浮上來。用手或手持攪拌機拌回去即可。
不需要，櫥櫃那個數字本來就是以不冷藏為前提。冷藏能延緩分離，但會變得非常難抹。
